name: Zamba-7B
attention_variant: hybrid: Mamba-2 backbone with a SINGLE SHARED attention block, invoked at 13 of 76 layers; MHA not GQA (16 query heads, 16 KV heads)
notes:
GEOMETRY FILLED from config.json, and the serving point is the shared block. num_hidden_layers 76, hidden_size 3712, num_attention_heads 16, num_key_value_heads 16, sliding_window null, rope_theta 10000, max_position_embeddings 4096. head_dim is NOT in config; it is hidden_size / num_attention_heads = 3712/16 = 232, an unusually wide head. gqa_ratio = 16/16 = 1.0, so this is plain MHA - there is no GQA saving anywhere in it. layers_block_type enumerates all 76 blocks: 63 mamba + 13 hybrid, the hybrid blocks at 0-based indices 2,7,13,19,25,31,37,43,49,55,61,67,73 (attn_layer_offset 4, attn_layer_period 6 - note the config's own periodicity formula does NOT reproduce the shipped layers_block_type array, so the array is authoritative). kv_cache_bytes_per_token = 13 hybrid invocations x 16 kv_heads x head_dim 232 x 2 (K+V) x 2 bytes (bf16) = 193,024 B/token (188.5 KiB). IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THAT FIGURE, and the reason this is the shared block rather than 13 independent attention layers: transformers' ZambaAttentionDecoderLayer docstring states layer_idx is 'Used to distinguish Zamba's tied transformer layers', and modeling_zamba.py binds the shared attention weights across all hybrid blocks via the key-rewrite regex r"layers.(?!{layer_id}\.)\d+.shared_transf". Tied WEIGHTS do not necessarily mean a shared CACHE - the cache is indexed by the forward-pass layer_idx, so 13 separate cache entries is the expected behaviour and 193,024 is the defensible number. A reader sizing memory should still treat it as an upper bound: if an engine instead shares one cache entry across the tied blocks the figure drops to 14,848 B/token. I could not confirm which a given engine does from config alone. The other 63 layers carry a constant Mamba-2 state instead: mamba_n_heads 2, mamba_d_state 16, mamba_d_conv 4, mamba_expand 2, mamba_dt_rank 232.
